name: CISO write gate is not diff-aware and gives no location: a comment-only fix of its own finding can never be written
description:
## Defect (found on card 675c4695, shift 3)

`project_write_file` refuses a whole-file write with:

```
Write blocked by CISO: block | high | 1 finding(s) | injection. Rules: injection.hidden-html-comment
```

even when the write **removes** the flagged comment.

### Evidence (reproducible)

Target: `client/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue` (631 lines, +123/-0 vs HEAD). Three variants were written, differing only in the flagged block at lines 183-185:

1. neutral, non-imperative prose;
2. a label-only marker `<!-- ── Repeat (recurrence) ── -->`, same kind as the `── Identity ──` / `── Assistant ──` markers already in the file;
3. the comment **deleted** (net -3 lines).

All three returned the identical `Write blocked by CISO: block | high | 1 finding(s) | injection`. `project_changes` afterwards still reports `+123/-0`, i.e. nothing was written and the block is not a partial-write artefact.

### Why this is a gate defect and not a finding

- The verdict is computed over the **whole file content**, not over the diff: removing the only flagged comment does not clear it. `security_review_changes` (diff-based) reported exactly 1 finding at `:183`, which the write gate contradicts.
- The error carries **no path:line and no snippet**, so the operator cannot tell which comment triggered it. The remaining candidates are the `<template>` comments inside the `+123` diff, most plausibly `:160-162` (`wake_at` is the alarm clock of the autonomy worker...).
- Net effect: any `.vue` that contains a hidden HTML comment the scanner dislikes becomes **unmodifiable through the write path**, including the edit that would fix it. That is a deadlock: the gate blocks its own remediation.

### Expected behaviour

1. Blame the offending `path:line` in the error (and the snippet), like `security_review_changes` does.
2. Evaluate the change being introduced, not the pre-existing content: a write that deletes or rewords the flagged comment must pass.
3. If the whole-content scan is intentional, expose a documented, audited way to write a remediation (e.g. an explicit acknowledgement argument recording who accepted what), instead of an unconditional refusal.

### Notes

- Distinct from `3a86fba9` (no patch-granularity write). A patch tool would not help here: the gate refuses the write itself, at any granularity.
- The fix lives in the platform backend (CISO guard around the file-write tool), which is outside this project's tool root (`.../codx-junior-platform/client`) - same limitation already recorded on `8a554fa4`. Whoever takes it needs a tool root at the repository root.
- Until it is fixed, card `675c4695` stays open in Working with its acceptance unmet.

### Acceptance

- A write that removes/rewords the flagged comment in `TaskSettings.vue` succeeds and `project_changes` shows a hunk limited to lines 183-185.
- A write that still contains an offending comment fails with `path:line` + snippet in the message.

## Measurement added (shift 3, from card 675c4695)

The failure mode is worse than "not diff-aware", so the diagnosis can be pinned down:

`TaskSettings.vue` holds **11 HTML comment blocks** (6-13, 16, 44, 90, 135-137, 183-185, 250, 255, 307-309, 329). Three observed writes:

| variant of 183-185 | result |
|---|---|
| neutral, non-imperative prose | `block`, **1 finding**, no location |
| label-only marker | `block`, **1 finding**, no location |
| comment **deleted** entirely | `block`, **1 finding**, no location |

Deleting the flagged block still leaves 1 finding, so **at least one other HTML comment also matches `injection.hidden-html-comment`** and the reported finding is not necessarily the one the user/agent set out to fix. Without `path:line` + snippet the operator cannot tell which one it is; with a whole-file-only writer the only "fix" available is a blind rewrite of all comments in a 631-line SFC, which risks dropping code.

### Requested behaviour (unchanged, now with a test)
- Every finding carries `path`, `line` and a 1-line snippet.
- The verdict is computed on the **diff** being written/committed, so a write that removes or neutralises the offending comment passes.
- When several comments match, report **all** of them (count ≥ 2 on this file), not a deduplicated count of 1 per rule.

### Reproduction case
Any write to `client/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue` from this project (root `.../codx-junior-platform/client`), vendor-free, no behaviour change intended.

## Shift 4 increment — the missing `path:line` localized, and why the gate's finding count proves nothing

**Changed files: none.** This card is a defect of the platform *write path* (the CISO guard around `project_write_file`), which lives outside this project's tool root. Re-verified this shift instead of assumed:

- `project_read_file("../api/pyproject.toml")` → `Path must belong to …/codx-junior-platform/client or to a linked project (read_project_dependencies …)`
- `read_folder("/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform")` → `Invalid path parameter: Path … is not within project root '…/client'`
- `project_read_file("/…/codx-junior-platform/api/pyproject.toml")` → `File not found`

So the guard cannot be read, patched or unit-tested from here. What *is* measurable from here is its input — which is exactly what the gate refuses to report.

### 1. Complete candidate set in the target file (the data the error omits)

`project_read_file("src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue", pattern="<!--")` → **10 hidden HTML comment blocks, all still on disk**:

| lines | kind | in the current diff? |
|---|---|---|
| 6-13 | prose: "── Properties dialog ── The fields of a chat/task, grouped in the three decisions the user actually makes…" | pre-existing |
| 16, 44, 90, 250, 255, 329 | one-line label markers (`── Identity ──`, `Header …`, `Footer …`) | pre-existing |
| **135-137** | **prose, same class as the finding: "`wake_at` is the alarm clock of the autonomy worker, not a deadline … Setting it moves the task to the after-hours shift and draws it in the calendar."** | **pre-existing** |
| **183-185** | **the reported one: "… `wake_at` is armed to the next occurrence; the autonomy runtime re-arms it after every run."** | **added (+123)** |
| 307-309 | prose: "── Danger zone … the destructive action is visible, but a single misclick cannot delete the conversation." | pre-existing |

`project_changes(scope="all", paths=["src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue"], include_patch=true)` → still `+123/-0`, three hunks (`@@ -180,4 +180,68 @@`, `@@ -321,4 +385,15 @@`, `@@ -503,4 +578,52 @@`). Nothing has been written since the three blocked variants, so the file state is unchanged and `:183` is an added line.

### 2. Why the card's "≥2 comments match" inference needs restating

- The **diff-based** review could only ever report `:183`: the first hunk starts at line 180, so `:135-137` is outside every hunk. A review count of 1 says nothing about how many matches exist in the *file*.
- The **write gate** scans the file content, so at `:135-137` it sees a block of the same class as the one it flags. Either it matches it (→ count should be ≥2) or it evaluated the **on-disk** content and never looked at the proposed one (→ 1 is the pre-existing `:183`). Both are consistent with `1 finding(s)`; nothing in the current evidence chooses between them.
- Class is set by the rule name and confirmed by content: the same sentences exist as `//` comments at `src/api/modules/chats.js:87-89` ("…the autonomy runtime re-arms it after every run…") and `injection.hidden-html-comment` does not cover JS comments. The trigger is *being hidden in the template*, not being addressed at the agent.

Consequence for `675c4695`: rewording **only** `:183-185` will very likely still be refused — which is what all three blocked variants observed. A remediation write must neutralise every prose block (6-13, 135-137, 183-185, 307-309), i.e. ~14 comment lines, and it must not be attempted by retyping 631 lines (see `3a86fba9`).

### 3. Acceptance refined for whoever owns the guard (needs a repo-root tool root)

1. Error carries `path:line` + one-line snippet for **each** match — no `1 finding(s)` aggregate. Without this the two hypotheses above stay indistinguishable, so this is a prerequisite, not a nicety.
2. Verdict computed on the **proposed content**: a proposed `TaskSettings.vue` with 6-13 / 135-137 / 183-185 / 307-309 neutralised must return `allow`; the unchanged file must still `block`.
3. Scanner-level regression test (no repo needed): (a) current template with only `:183` removed → the report must list the remaining matches individually (this is the test that proves whether the count is deduplicated); (b) all four prose blocks removed → `0 findings`.
4. `3a86fba9` does **not** unblock this: the refusal happens at whole-content scan, at any write granularity. The two fixes are independent.

**Validation evidence available this shift: none executable.** This runtime has no shell and no node (`91411767`, `3a86fba9`), so no test command can be run; every statement above is a tool output (paths, line numbers, unchanged diff) reproduced here. No file was modified by this increment.

Moving to **Review** — status stays `doing`, I do not close my own cards.

## Shift 6 (turn 3) increment — acceptance #3 is already shipped: the escape hatch exists, is persisted and is named in the gate's own error

**Changed files: none.** This increment is evidence gathering inside the reachable tree (`client/`); the guard itself is still outside my tool root. What is new is that the card's central claim — *"there is no documented, audited way to write a remediation"* — is **false as written**, and that changes what the fix has to be.

### 1. A documented, persisted, audited remediation path already exists

| Evidence | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `src/api/modules/ciso.js:92-95` — `/** Enable or silence one rule (persisted in the project policy). */ setRule(ruleId, enabled) { return API.put('/api/ciso/rules/' + ruleId, { enabled }) }` | Silencing a rule is a first-class API, project-scoped (the connection adds `codx_path`). |
| `src/api/modules/ciso.js:100-110` — `policy()` / `updatePolicy(changes)` / `resetPolicy()` | The whole policy is readable and editable as a validated partial; `resetPolicy` reverts. |
| `src/components/ciso/CisoRules.vue:6-8` — *"the detector catalogue … can be silenced one by one; the toggle writes the project `ciso_policy.ignore_rules`, and **the very next gate in the process honours it**"* | This is the product's own written contract: the policy governs the gate, including the write gate. The defect is therefore a **contract violation**, not a missing feature. |
| `src/components/ciso/CisoRules.vue:113` — `ignore_paths: [...(policy.ignore_paths || [])]` | A second, narrower lever: exclude a path instead of a rule. |
| `src/components/ciso/CisoRules.vue:180` — *"Policy saved: the next gate uses it immediately."* (emitted after `updatePolicy`) | No restart, no redeploy needed. |
| `src/components/ciso/CisoRules.vue:210-222` — `toggleRule(rule)` → `setRule(rule.rule_id, !rule.enabled)` | The exact call shape, from the UI. |
| `src/components/ciso/format.js:22` — `injection: 'Prompt injection'` (`DOMAIN_LABELS`) | `injection.hidden-html-comment` is `<domain>.<rule>`; the `injection` domain is a real catalogue domain, i.e. the rule in the gate message is a **toggleable catalogue entry**, not an unnamed internal check. |

Consequence: the string in the refusal (`Rules: injection.hidden-html-comment`) is itself the exact `rule_id` to feed to `setRule`, and the refusal is writable-off **from the product UI** (CISO → Rules → toggle off, do the edit, toggle back). Two cli-free remediations exist today:

- **narrow:** `PUT /api/ciso/policy {"ignore_paths": ["…/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue"]}` while the comment is removed, then remove the entry;
- **broad:** `PUT /api/ciso/rules/injection.hidden-html-comment {"enabled": false}`, edit, re-enable.

### 2. What that leaves of the defect (unchanged, and still worth fixing)

1. **No `path:line`** in the refusal → the operator still cannot tell *which* comment, so the "reword it instead of silencing the rule" path is blind. The count is also useless: the diff-based scan reported 1 finding at `:183` while the card's own analysis finds 5 candidate blocks (`6-13`, `135-137`, `183-185`, `307-309`) — either the whole-content scan **deduplicates**, or it scans a different text. That contradiction is now the primary open question.
2. **Diff-unawareness** (a write that *removes* the finding still blocks) is real and unrefuted by this increment — but note it is *policy-tunable*: the ladder in `editableProjection` (`enabled`, `block_above`, `approval_above`, `warn_above`, `block_categories`, `strict_domains`, `fail_closed` — `CisoRules.vue:74-99`) means a gate that evaluates the *proposal* would be a behaviour change to the guard, not a new knob.
3. Silence is **global to the project**: silencing `injection` for one comment removal disables that detector for every file until it is toggled back. That is why the acceptance should prefer `path:line` + diff-awareness over "silence and remember to re-enable".

### 3. Corrected acceptance proposal (supersedes mine from shift 4)

- **A (must):** a write whose proposed content no longer contains the flagged block is **allowed** and `project_changes` shows a hunk limited to the flagged lines.
- **B (must):** a write whose proposed content still contains an offending block **fails** and the message carries `path:line` + ≤160-char excerpt (the excerpt limit already exists in policy: `max_excerpt_chars`, `CisoRules.vue:118`).
- **C (must, cheap, decides the dedup question):** one run of the whole-content scan on `TaskSettings.vue` as it currently stands must **list every match individually**; if it does not, the finding count is not a match count and the funnel on `b7225e63`/`acc01b1f` inherits the flaw.
- **D (nice):** the refusal names the remediation (`silence rule <id>` / `ignore_paths`) so the next operator does not have to reverse-engineer it.

### 4. Validation evidence

- **No executable command exists in this runtime** (no shell, no `node` — `91411767`, `3a86fba9`), so nothing was run and no test result is claimed. Every statement above is a quoted `file:line` from the reachable tree, reproduced verbatim.
- **No write was attempted this shift.** I deliberately did **not** probe the guard with a throwaway file: this runtime has no delete/exec tool, and a probe file that *is* allowed would stay in the tree forever (exactly the defect on `61098a6b`). The discrimination test is therefore written down, not executed.
- **The one test that decides it** (needs an `api/`-rooted agent, one call, no code change): silence the rule via `PUT /api/ciso/rules/injection.hidden-html-comment {"enabled": false}`, retry the `TaskSettings.vue` write. Allowed ⇒ the guard consults `ignore_rules` and the remaining bug is only diff-awareness + `path:line`. Still blocked ⇒ the guard bypasses the policy and violates the `CisoRules.vue:6-8` contract, which is the sharper bug to file.

Cross-posted to `675c4695`, which is blocked by this and can now be unblocked from the product UI instead of waiting for a platform fix. Moving this card to **Review**, status stays `doing`; I do not close my own cards.

## Correction to my own comment above (measured after posting it) — the "contract" is untracked work, not shipped behaviour

I verified the working tree at the end of the shift (`project_changes(scope="all", paths=["src","tests","package.json"])`, 110 files, +9753/−952) and every file I cited as *"the product's written contract"* is **untracked** (`?`, i.e. not in `HEAD`):

```
? src/api/modules/ciso.js
? src/components/ciso/CisoActivity.vue
? src/components/ciso/CisoFindings.vue
? src/components/ciso/CisoOverview.vue
? src/components/ciso/CisoRules.vue
? src/components/ciso/CisoScans.vue
? src/components/ciso/format.js
? src/views/CisoView.vue
```

What that changes, precisely:

- **Still true:** the mechanism exists in the tree, is documented in writing, and is one API call away (`setRule` → `PUT /api/ciso/rules/{ruleId}`, `updatePolicy` → `PUT /api/ciso/policy`). The refusal names the exact `rule_id` to silence, and `injection` is a declared domain (`format.js:22`). The two remediations stand as **procedure**.
- **Must be softened:** *"the gate violates its documented contract"* is **not** established. The contract lives in an **uncommitted** feature (whole CISO view + API module untracked), so the server-side guard and the policy plumbing may simply be of different vintages, or the guard may predate `ignore_rules` entirely. Calling it a contract violation before running the test would be asserting more than the evidence allows.
- **Unchanged:** the discrimination test I wrote (silence the rule → retry the write) is still the one cheap call that decides it, and it is still **not executed** here — no `api`-rooted tool, no shell, no `node`.
- **New, reproducible fact worth carrying:** the whole CISO subsystem is **uncommitted** (8 untracked files, one of them `src/api/modules/ciso.js`). Any statement about what the gate "should" do inherits that instability — and it means the guard fix and the CISO feature cannot be reviewed in one diff. Logged on `e24eac3e`, which owns the "uncommitted features" problem.

I would rather hand over a narrower, correct claim than the sharper one I posted three minutes ago. Acceptance proposal (A/B/C/D) and the Review move are unchanged.

## QA gate — Decision: require_approval

- **Scope:** `paths=["client/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue"]`, `scope=all`, base `HEAD`
- **Evidence:** changed_files **1** (examined), mapped_sources **0**, unmapped_sources **1**; tests executed **0** (runner dead: `pytest` exit 1 / 0 collected; `npm` absent)
- **Findings:** 1 — `change.missing-tests` (medium, `TaskSettings.vue`)
- **Failing test ids:** none — nothing executed.
- **Card acceptance NOT met, on both criteria:**
  1. A write that rewrites/removes the flagged comment at `TaskSettings.vue:183-185` **still does not land** — the card itself records three variants (neutral prose, label-only marker, comment deleted) all returning the identical block, with `project_changes` unchanged at +123/-0. Verified again this shift: the comment is **still at lines 183–185**.
  2. "A write that still contains an offending comment fails with `path:line` + snippet" — unverifiable; the CISO gate is not diff-aware and reports no location, which is the defect this card describes.
- **Blocking item:** the write gate must (a) let a comment-only edit of its own finding through, and (b) fail with `path:line` + snippet when the offence remains. Neither is demonstrable today.
- **Owner:** `software_developer` (CISO write gate). QA cannot verify a security tool's behaviour it cannot trigger — and `security_review_changes` is additionally broken by `8a554fa4` (path root) and `b7225e63` (timeout).
- **Next command:** `qa_review_changes(paths=["client/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue"], scope="all")` **plus** a CISO write attempt whose `project_changes` hunk is limited to lines 183–185.

Moving back to **Working**.
